DeForest's labor & Employment practice advises employers whose workforce stability is fundamental to business continuity. Acting as strategic counsel to multinational and domestic companies, the team combines labor advisory, litigation, collective labor relations, social security, compliance and workforce governance into a fully integrated national platform capable of supporting complex operations throughout Mexico.
Rather than approaching labor law as a reactive discipline, the practice helps employers anticipate labor risk, strengthen governance frameworks and preserve operational continuity throughout the entire employment lifecycle—from hiring and day-to-day advisory to collective bargaining, workforce restructurings, regulatory inspections, social security matters and high-value litigation.
The practice has developed particular strength advising companies operating in highly regulated and labor-intensive industries, including automotive, advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, logistics, retail, technology, telecommunications and financial services, where employment strategy directly affects production continuity, investment certainty and long-term business performance.
The department is led by one of the country's most experienced labor teams. Eduardo Garduño has become one of Mexico's leading labor strategists for multinational employers, combining more than two decades of experience advising major corporations with senior public-sector insight that enables him to translate complex regulatory environments into practical business solutions.
Jaime Bustamante contributes the perspective of one of the region's largest employers, having previously served as Legal Director for Mexico, Central and South America at ManpowerGroup, where he oversaw workforce structures across multiple jurisdictions.
Raymundo Carreño brings the institutional knowledge accumulated during nearly four decades as General Legal Director of Volkswagen de México, offering clients strategic judgement developed through some of the country's most significant labor negotiations and organisational transformations.
The leadership team is further strengthened by Javier Atzin Vallejo, whose practice focuses on labor compliance, social security and workforce integration; Edgar Barreto, recognised for his experience in labor litigation and IMSS matters; Andrés Cabrera, who leads the firm's labor practice across the Bajío region; Erick Pérez, a specialist in complex litigation and constitutional proceedings; and José Alberto Díaz, whose practice combines labor, social security and administrative litigation in highly regulated industries.
Today the practice advises employers whose combined workforce exceeds one million employees throughout Mexico. Its work extends well beyond litigation management and encompasses nationwide litigation portfolios involving hundreds of simultaneous proceedings, including approximately 700 labor disputes managed by the firm's Puebla team. The practice also advises on collective bargaining negotiations, union representation disputes, labor integration following mergers and acquisitions, employer restructurings, labor and social security audits, constitutional litigation, preventive governance programmes and regulatory inspections before the Ministry of Labor, IMSS and INFONAVIT.
Clients consistently retain DeForest not simply to resolve labor disputes, but to preserve organisational stability in environments where workforce disruption could directly affect production, investment and corporate reputation. This preventive, business-oriented philosophy has positioned the practice among Mexico's leading advisers to multinational employers navigating increasingly sophisticated labor challenges.
During the last twelve months alone, the team has also assisted more than twenty clients in connection with labor inspections conducted by the Ministry of labor and has handled numerous audits involving labor and social security compliance, reinforcing its position as trusted counsel for employers operating in highly regulated sectors.
The firm's sustained growth is reflected in its recognition by Chambers Latin America 2025 for General Business Law (Querétaro), The Legal 500 since 2024 for labor & Employment and IFLR1000 2025 for Corporate & M&A, confirming the continued consolidation of DeForest as one of Mexico's most sophisticated full-service business law firms.

lawyers.bio:
Eduardo is the Partner of DeForest’s Labor & Employment practice and one of the most respected voices in labor governance in Mexico. His background blends more than two decades advising multinational employers with senior public-sector experience, allowing him to translate complex regulatory environments into stable operational frameworks. He is known for structuring policies and documentation systems that support high-risk, labor-intensive operations, as well as for steering high-value disputes that require strategic judgement and procedural precision. His leadership extends across mandates involving litigation coordination, cross-state governance and preventive frameworks for clients such as Volkswagen, Cinemex, GeNi, Scheaffler, Benteler, SKF and Megacable.
He regularly delivers conferences on labor developments and legal updates at CLAUZ, CANACINTRA and the American Chamber of Commerce in Guadalajara, as well as at universities including Universidad Anáhuac Puebla.
He serves as President of the labor Committee of ANADE Puebla and actively participates in various labor forums, including business chambers.

matters.title: Confidential Matter 1
matters.summary:
Mextypsa, one of Mexico's leading engineering and infrastructure companies, relies on DeForest as its strategic labor counsel for projects where workforce governance is fundamental to successful execution. The firm's mandate extends beyond day-to-day employment advice, encompassing the design of labor structures capable of supporting large-scale infrastructure projects while preserving regulatory compliance and operational continuity throughout each project's lifecycle.

One of the most significant engagements involved the Guadalajara Metro Line 4 Project, a USD 552 million infrastructure development requiring a sophisticated labor framework to manage project-based recruitment, documentation, workforce administration and eventual demobilisation under intense public scrutiny. Simultaneously, DeForest represented the client in complex litigation arising from the Coahuila Wind Farm Project, where an adverse labor judgment threatened liabilities exceeding MXN 5.5 million.

Rather than treating these matters as isolated engagements, DeForest developed a comprehensive labor governance strategy combining preventive advisory with high-stakes dispute resolution. The team designed the contractual and compliance architecture supporting the Guadalajara Metro project, supervised workforce demobilisation to minimise post-project contingencies and successfully challenged the adverse labor judgment through constitutional proceedings, restoring the client's procedural rights and reopening the litigation.

Today, the firm manages more than twenty labor disputes for Mextypsa representing aggregate exposure of approximately MXN 21.5 million. Through early negotiation strategies and disciplined litigation management, DeForest has consistently reduced financial exposure while protecting operational continuity across the client's infrastructure portfolio.

matters.title: Confidential Matter 2
matters.summary:
Bonatti has entrusted DeForest with the labor governance strategy supporting several of Mexico's largest energy infrastructure projects, where uninterrupted workforce stability is essential to the successful execution of multi-billion-dollar developments. Acting as strategic labor counsel, the firm advises throughout the entire project lifecycle, integrating labor compliance, collective employment matters and litigation strategy into a single governance framework.

The mandate includes the Energía Mayakan Pipeline Expansion, valued at more than USD 2 billion, the Cuxtal II expansion, the Ojinaga-El Encino Gas Pipeline and strategic operational support for ENI México's energy projects in Tabasco.

DeForest designed and implemented the labor architecture supporting each project, including workforce documentation, project-specific employment structures, compliance programmes, dispute prevention strategies and workforce demobilisation. Alongside this preventive work, the firm managed more than twenty labor disputes arising during project execution, resolving the overwhelming majority through conciliation and reducing potential financial exposure by approximately eighty percent.

The team also prevented an imminent strike that threatened to halt operations linked to Mexico's strategic energy infrastructure, safeguarding contractual performance, operational continuity and the client's long-term commercial position. Today, DeForest acts not simply as litigation counsel but as a long-term strategic partner supporting some of the country's most critical infrastructure developments.

matters.title: Confidential Matter 3
matters.summary:
Following Schaeffler's global acquisition of Vitesco Technologies, DeForest was appointed to lead one of the most significant post-acquisition labor integration projects currently underway in Mexico. The transaction required the harmonisation of employment structures across multiple manufacturing facilities while ensuring uninterrupted operations throughout the integration process.

The firm designed and implemented the labor integration strategy affecting facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labor governance policies for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees.

Parallel to the integration, DeForest manages thirty-five active labor proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, ensuring that litigation strategy remains fully aligned with the client's unified post-acquisition governance model. Through this combination of workforce integration, compliance and litigation management, the firm has become a long-term strategic adviser supporting one of the world's leading automotive suppliers.

matters.title: Confidential Matter 5
matters.summary:
Nueva Empresa, S.C. engaged DeForest in two high-value wrongful termination proceedings that raised issues extending well beyond financial exposure. Following procedural objections concerning the legal standing of the company's attorney-in-fact, the labor court refused to recognise the company's representation, disregarded its defence and issued an adverse ruling despite the existence of valid notarial documentation confirming the attorney's legal identity.

The dispute presented a significant constitutional question concerning due process, legal certainty and the recognition of legally valid identity changes, creating an important opportunity to clarify procedural standards within Mexico's labor justice system.

DeForest challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the labor court's interpretation violated the client's due process rights and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney's legal standing and restored the client's right to present its defence.

Beyond the financial exposure of approximately MXN 3 million, the matter is significant for reinforcing constitutional protections governing procedural fairness and the legal recognition of identity, establishing an important precedent with broader implications for labor litigation in Mexico.

DeForest designed and implemented the client's negotiation and litigation strategy, guiding the company through complex union representation proceedings while preserving uninterrupted operations. Through proactive dialogue and careful procedural management, the firm successfully prevented work stoppages and avoided escalation under the USMCA Rapid Response labor Mechanism, protecting both operational continuity and the client's long-term industrial stability.

The matter demonstrates DeForest's ability to navigate one of the most challenging aspects of Mexico's post-reform labor landscape, combining collective bargaining expertise with strategic business risk management.

matters.summary:
One of Mexico's most extraordinary labor disputes gave rise to this engagement. A former senior executive obtained a labor judgment exceeding MXN 2.162 billion, exposing Enerflex and indirectly PEMEX to unprecedented financial and governance risks. Against this exceptional backdrop, the employee retained DeForest to develop an alternative strategy capable of unlocking negotiations that had reached complete deadlock.

Rather than relying exclusively on litigation, DeForest designed a parallel mediation strategy running alongside the judicial proceedings. The firm established common valuation criteria, governance-based negotiation parameters and structured settlement mechanisms capable of facilitating constructive dialogue between parties that had previously been unwilling to negotiate.

The strategy ultimately generated a series of favourable settlement agreements that preserved the employee's legitimate interests while significantly reducing systemic exposure for Enerflex and preventing PEMEX from facing joint liability arising from one of the largest labor awards ever issued in Mexico. The matter remains ongoing, with DeForest continuing to coordinate negotiations alongside PEMEX's in-house legal team.

This engagement reflects the firm's ability to resolve disputes where legal complexity, commercial interests and public-sector exposure intersect at the highest level.

Rather than addressing disputes individually, the firm has implemented a coordinated labor strategy that combines litigation management with preventive advisory, enabling the client to maintain consistent employment standards across multiple jurisdictions.

The engagement demonstrates DeForest's ability to provide scalable labor governance solutions for employers operating large, decentralised workforces in highly regulated industries.

matters.summary:
SEBNMX, an automotive manufacturer employing approximately 2,000 people in Tlaxcala, engaged DeForest to modernise the legal framework supporting one of its principal manufacturing operations. The mandate arose within the context of Mexico's labor reform, requiring the client to strengthen its employment governance while maintaining uninterrupted industrial operations.

DeForest conducted a comprehensive review of the client's labor governance platform, updating internal workplace regulations, employment agreements, labor policies and mixed commissions while supporting the implementation of the latest labor reform requirements. The engagement focused on ensuring that the client's employment framework remained operationally effective, legally compliant and capable of supporting a large industrial workforce.

By integrating legal compliance with practical workforce governance, the firm strengthened the client's long-term organisational resilience while reducing regulatory exposure.

matters.summary:
SCOTCH engaged DeForest to review and restructure its corporate and labor framework following the introduction of Mexico's specialised services regime (REPSE). The matter required a multidisciplinary approach combining labor, corporate and regulatory expertise to ensure that the client's business model remained fully aligned with the country's evolving outsourcing framework.

Working jointly across its corporate and labor practices, DeForest carried out a comprehensive review of the client's corporate structure, specialised services model, bylaws and REPSE registration while simultaneously conducting an audit of more than eighty suppliers to determine the appropriate regulatory treatment of specialised services agreements.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's ability to advise clients on complex regulatory transformations where employment, corporate governance and commercial operations converge.

Grupo Solana, a diversified automotive and real estate group employing more than 1,200 people, retained DeForest to implement a complex employer substitution process affecting its workforce structure. The matter required careful coordination between labor and regulatory authorities to ensure business continuity while restructuring the group's employment platform.

DeForest designed and executed the legal strategy necessary to reactivate the employer registration that had previously been cancelled, allowing the employer substitution process to proceed without disrupting the client's operations. The firm coordinated the labor transition while ensuring full compliance with applicable employment regulations and preserving workforce stability throughout the restructuring.

The engagement illustrates the firm's ability to support complex corporate reorganisations where labor law plays a critical role in enabling business transformation.

The project required the separation of business functions, the redesign of the group's employment model and the creation of a specialised services platform aligned with Mexico's post-outsourcing regulatory framework.

DeForest developed the legal strategy supporting the group's restructuring, including the creation of a specialised services entity, employer substitution processes, the redesign of corporate purposes and the implementation of a workforce transition affecting multiple operating companies. In parallel, the firm represents the client in social security litigation before the Federal Court of Administrative Justice challenging tax assessments relating to two manufacturing facilities, while continuing to advise on broader labor and social security governance matters.

The engagement reflects the firm's ability to coordinate multidisciplinary projects where labor law, corporate restructuring and social security litigation converge to support large-scale business transformation.

DeForest's labor & Employment practice advises employers whose workforce stability is fundamental to business continuity. Acting as strategic counsel to multinational and domestic companies, the team combines labor advisory, litigation, collective labor relations, social security, compliance and workforce governance into a fully integrated national platform capable of supporting complex operations throughout Mexico.
Rather than approaching labor law as a reactive discipline, the practice helps employers anticipate labor risk, strengthen governance frameworks and preserve operational continuity throughout the entire employment lifecycle—from hiring and day-to-day advisory to collective bargaining, workforce restructurings, regulatory inspections, social security matters and high-value litigation.
The practice has developed particular strength advising companies operating in highly regulated and labor-intensive industries, including automotive, advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, logistics, retail, technology, telecommunications and financial services, where employment strategy directly affects production continuity, investment certainty and long-term business performance.
The department is led by one of the country's most experienced labor teams. Eduardo Garduño has become one of Mexico's leading labor strategists for multinational employers, combining more than two decades of experience advising major corporations with senior public-sector insight that enables him to translate complex regulatory environments into practical business solutions.
Jaime Bustamante contributes the perspective of one of the region's largest employers, having previously served as Legal Director for Mexico, Central and South America at ManpowerGroup, where he oversaw workforce structures across multiple jurisdictions.
Raymundo Carreño brings the institutional knowledge accumulated during nearly four decades as General Legal Director of Volkswagen de México, offering clients strategic judgement developed through some of the country's most significant labor negotiations and organisational transformations.
The leadership team is further strengthened by Javier Atzin Vallejo, whose practice focuses on labor compliance, social security and workforce integration; Edgar Barreto, recognised for his experience in labor litigation and IMSS matters; Andrés Cabrera, who leads the firm's labor practice across the Bajío region; Erick Pérez, a specialist in complex litigation and constitutional proceedings; and José Alberto Díaz, whose practice combines labor, social security and administrative litigation in highly regulated industries.
Today the practice advises employers whose combined workforce exceeds one million employees throughout Mexico. Its work extends well beyond litigation management and encompasses nationwide litigation portfolios involving hundreds of simultaneous proceedings, including approximately 700 labor disputes managed by the firm's Puebla team. The practice also advises on collective bargaining negotiations, union representation disputes, labor integration following mergers and acquisitions, employer restructurings, labor and social security audits, constitutional litigation, preventive governance programmes and regulatory inspections before the Ministry of Labor, IMSS and INFONAVIT.
Clients consistently retain DeForest not simply to resolve labor disputes, but to preserve organisational stability in environments where workforce disruption could directly affect production, investment and corporate reputation. This preventive, business-oriented philosophy has positioned the practice among Mexico's leading advisers to multinational employers navigating increasingly sophisticated labor challenges.
During the last twelve months alone, the team has also assisted more than twenty clients in connection with labor inspections conducted by the Ministry of labor and has handled numerous audits involving labor and social security compliance, reinforcing its position as trusted counsel for employers operating in highly regulated sectors.
The firm's sustained growth is reflected in its recognition by Chambers Latin America 2025 for General Business Law (Querétaro), The Legal 500 since 2024 for labor & Employment and IFLR1000 2025 for Corporate & M&A, confirming the continued consolidation of DeForest as one of Mexico's most sophisticated full-service business law firms.

**Portafolio recomendado — core, en orden estratégico.** Todos los asuntos seleccionados tienen decisión de confidencialidad confirmada y deben ir en la sección confidencial.

1. **SCHAEFFLER — hero.** Eduardo Garduño lideró la integración laboral post-adquisición en seis estados para más de 5.000 empleados, con armonización de documentación laboral y colectiva y alineación de 35 procedimientos activos.
2. **Brose México.** Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera la estrategia de negociación y litigio en una controversia de titularidad de contrato colectivo; la fuente atribuye la prevención de paros y la evitación de escalamiento bajo el USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism.
3. **GeNI de México.** Eduardo Garduño y Carlos Rivera lideraron negociación colectiva ante riesgo inminente de huelga; la fuente indica que el acuerdo evitó la huelga y preservó producción ininterrumpida.
4. **Coats de México.** Eduardo Garduño dirigió una transformación de fuerza laboral en Puebla, Veracruz y Tlaxcala, con documentación colectiva y negociaciones sindicales sobre exposición superior a MXN 12,5 millones.
5. **Cinemex.** Eduardo Garduño y Fernanda Priego encabezan una plataforma nacional de aproximadamente 200 procedimientos activos, conciliaciones, restructuraciones y medidas preventivas para una plantilla de más de 11.000 personas.
6. **Volkswagen de México y VW Financial Services.** Eduardo Garduño lidera la gestión integrada de procedimientos con exposición agregada cercana a MXN 280 millones y asesoría de gobernanza laboral preventiva.
7. **Poliuretanos Summa Woodbridge.** José Alberto Díaz Méndez lidera una restructuración de aproximadamente ocho sociedades, con entidad de servicios especializados, sustituciones patronales y litigio de seguridad social pendiente.
8. **Bonatti.** Javier Atzin Vallejo lidera arquitectura laboral de proyectos energéticos, más de 20 controversias y prevención de una huelga inminente; el resultado de conciliación y reducción aproximada de exposición debe mantenerse separado de los valores de los proyectos.

letter.executive_assessment:
**Veredicto ejecutivo — presentar para primera inclusión.** La propuesta actual sostiene una candidatura coherente de Labour & Employment employer-side en México, sin solicitar ni insinuar una banda concreta. El objetivo se apoya en una combinación poco redundante de integración post-adquisición, relaciones colectivas y disputas de representatividad, carteras de litigio laboral, restructuraciones patronales, cumplimiento REPSE y seguridad social. La investigación oficial disponible no identificó una coincidencia exacta de DeForest Abogados ni de los abogados nominados en la tabla de Chambers Latin America consultada; ello no acredita ausencia de ranking fuera de ese alcance. La comparación externa es limitada: se recuperaron perfiles de tres firmas Band 5, útiles como contexto de que el mercado reconoce una mezcla de negociación colectiva, litigio individual/colectivo, asesoría laboral y seguridad social, pero insuficientes para una calibración completa o una predicción de posición.

La principal fortaleza demostrativa es la concentración de trabajo directamente atribuido a Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo y Jaime Bustamante, junto con evidencia de ejecución nacional y en sectores industriales. SCHAEFFLER debe mantenerse como hero: reúne integración laboral posterior a adquisición, armonización de acuerdos y documentación laboral y colectiva en seis estados para más de 5.000 empleados, y coordinación de 35 procedimientos laborales activos; Eduardo Garduño figura como lead partner. Frente a Cinemex, que prueba mayor escala de litigio, SCHAEFFLER ofrece la combinación más completa de transformación laboral, implementación multiestatal, relaciones colectivas y liderazgo individual atribuible.

La vulnerabilidad principal no es la relevancia jurídica de los asuntos, sino la dependencia de narrativas internas de mandatos confidenciales y la evidencia individual desigual fuera de los tres líderes principales. La ausencia de ventana de investigación y de fechas en algunos asuntos es una advertencia de metadatos, no una razón para excluirlos ni para detener la presentación.

The firm’s preventive governance work was tested in three inspections conducted by the Ministry of Labor and IMSS. Those inspections concluded without fines despite combined potential exposure approaching MXN 2 million. Jaime Bustamante leads the ongoing mandate.

It integrates procedural strategy with commercial settlement discussions to contain overall financial risk. Jaime Bustamante leads the ongoing matter.

matters.text:
DeForest manages labour litigation and preventive employment governance for Securitas de México as the client expands operations across Puebla, Mexico City, Torreón and Veracruz. The mandate concerns a geographically dispersed workforce in the private-security sector.

The firm manages more than 50 labour proceedings involving aggregate exposure approaching MXN 10 million. It also advises on documentation, employment governance and risk mitigation across the client’s expanding national footprint, applying a coordinated approach to litigation and preventive advisory. Eduardo Garduño leads the mandate, supported by Maximiliano Hernández and Erick Pérez.

Rather than addressing disputes individually, the firm has implemented a coordinated labor strategy that combines litigation management with preventive advisory, enabling the client to maintain consistent employment standards across multiple jurisdictions.

candidates.submission_bio:
Eduardo Garduño leads DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice. He has led the labour integration following an automotive-sector acquisition, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labour-governance policies across six Mexican states for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees, while coordinating the alignment of 35 active labour proceedings with the post-acquisition governance model. He also leads collective bargaining and workforce-transformation mandates for industrial employers, including negotiations undertaken to address imminent strike risk and multi-facility restructuring.

His work includes nationwide litigation and employment-governance mandates for large employers, combining active labour proceedings with advice on employment documentation, disciplinary procedures, workplace regulations and preventive labour strategy. Eduardo also leads union-representation responses involving litigation, collective bargaining strategy and negotiations with competing unions.

comparisons.tradeoff: SEBNMX aportaría otra prueba clara de implementación de reforma laboral en manufactura. Se mantiene SCHAEFFLER porque prueba mejor escala, complejidad multiestatal, integración post-adquisición y liderazgo individual.
comparisons.incremental_contribution: SCHAEFFLER aporta una integración post-adquisición para más de 5,000 empleados en seis estados, documentación colectiva y 35 procedimientos activos, además de liderazgo atribuido a Eduardo Garduño. SEBNMX acredita una modernización laboral para aproximadamente 2,000 empleados, pero no añade litigio activo, documentación colectiva ni una transformación derivada de adquisición.

comparisons.tradeoff: REGSA reforzaría la continuidad entre gobernanza preventiva y representatividad. Brose se conserva porque acredita mayor fricción colectiva y un resultado específico de continuidad operativa.
comparisons.incremental_contribution: Brose añade una controversia sobre titularidad de contrato colectivo, prevención de paros y evitación de escalamiento bajo el USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism, liderada por Javier Atzin Vallejo. REGSA también aporta representatividad sindical, pero carece de un resultado operativo equivalente.

comparisons.tradeoff: American Axle añadiría evidencia de una relación automotriz reciente liderada por Jaime Bustamante. PSW se conserva por la mayor complejidad de reestructuración y por demostrar coordinación laboral, corporativa y de seguridad social.
comparisons.incremental_contribution: PSW aporta una reestructuración de aproximadamente ocho compañías, una entidad de servicios especializados, sustituciones patronales y litigio de seguridad social pendiente. American Axle aporta una nueva relación relevante y due diligence, pero su implementación permanece en curso y sin resultado documentado.

development.positioning: La identidad editorial más sólida es la de una práctica employer-side que protege la continuidad operativa de empleadores industriales y de infraestructura mediante una combinación de relaciones colectivas, transformación de la fuerza laboral, litigio laboral a escala y gobernanza preventiva. La selección muestra actividad en manufactura, automotriz, energía, infraestructura y operaciones de trabajo descentralizadas.
development.hero_rationale: SCHAEFFLER es el hero más demostrativo porque combina una integración laboral posterior a adquisición, ejecución en seis estados, armonización de documentación laboral y colectiva para más de 5,000 empleados y 35 procedimientos laborales activos, con Eduardo Garduño identificado como lead partner. Frente a la cartera de Cinemex, que acredita escala litigiosa, SCHAEFFLER demuestra una combinación más completa de transformación laboral, relaciones colectivas, implementación multiestatal y liderazgo individual atribuible.
development.target_rationale: El objetivo principal suministrado es primera inclusión y no existe un target de banda solicitado. La verificación oficial disponible no encontró una coincidencia exacta de la firma en la tabla consultada, lo que no acredita ausencia de ranking en otras ediciones o prácticas. La investigación externa recuperada ofrece contexto limitado de perfiles Band 5, pero no permite calibración completa ni predicción de una banda.
development.principal_strength: La selección reúne evidencia directamente relevante de relaciones colectivas, prevención de huelgas, disputas de representatividad sindical, integración post-adquisición de más de 5,000 empleados, carteras de litigios con aproximadamente 200 procedimientos activos y reestructuraciones laborales y de seguridad social complejas.
development.filing_recommendation: Presentar la candidatura para primera inclusión, con una narrativa concentrada en trabajo employer-side de alto impacto: integración laboral post-adquisición, relaciones colectivas y disputas de representatividad sindical, carteras nacionales de litigio, reestructuraciones y cumplimiento laboral y de seguridad social. No debe solicitarse ni insinuarse una banda concreta.
development.principal_vulnerability: La candidatura depende en gran medida de descripciones internas de mandatos confidenciales. Aunque la atribución de liderazgo es sólida para Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo y Jaime Bustamante, la evidencia individual para otros abogados del roster es escasa o no está vinculada a matters. Faltan también ventana de investigación y confirmación de actividad pertinente para algunos matters sin fechas.

strategy.thesis: The submitted evidence supports a first-time-recognition objective through a concentrated employer-side Labour & Employment narrative: post-acquisition workforce integration, collective bargaining and union-representation disputes, large-scale litigation portfolios, workforce restructurings, REPSE implementation and social-security governance. The strongest source-backed hero is SCHAEFFLER, a six-state post-acquisition integration affecting more than 5,000 employees and aligned litigation management, led by Eduardo Garduño. The core selection gives visible, source-attributed leadership to Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo, Jaime Bustamante and José Alberto Díaz Méndez, while retaining supporting matters for breadth. All selected matters have confirmed confidential status and therefore belong in the confidential section; public-facing prose must anonymise them and must not disclose Omron’s expressly confidential value. The available Chambers research is limited: the firm and named lawyers were not found in the scoped table, which does not establish that they are unranked, and competitor-profile evidence provides limited external context rather than a full market calibration. No rank or band is predicted.

matters.rationale: Core and hero: the evidence combines a major workforce integration, multi-state implementation, collective documentation and active litigation alignment, with Eduardo Garduño named as lead. Direct evidence: “The firm designed and implemented the labor integration strategy affecting facilities in Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua, standardising employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labor governance policies for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees.”

matters.legal_understanding: Post-acquisition labour integration following Schaeffler’s global acquisition of Vitesco Technologies. DeForest led integration of employment, collective-bargaining and governance documentation across facilities in six Mexican states for more than 5,000 employees, while managing 35 active labour proceedings. The matter’s status and monetary value are not supplied; the source describes it as currently underway.

editorial_development.c2:
DeForest seeks first-time recognition for its Labour & Employment practice in Mexico. The team advises employers on matters where collective labour relations, workforce transformation, litigation exposure and regulatory compliance directly affect operational continuity.

Its representative work includes post-acquisition integration across six states for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees; collective bargaining and union-representation matters in which the team prevented work stoppages; nationwide labour litigation portfolios involving approximately 200 active proceedings; and labour, union-related and social-security governance for an industrial workforce of approximately 17,000 employees. The practice also handles employer substitutions, REPSE-related restructuring, constitutional labour litigation, internal investigations and preventive inspection strategy.

The submission demonstrates a coherent employer-side practice combining contentious and non-contentious capability, with visible leadership from Eduardo Garduño, Javier Atzin Vallejo and Jaime Bustamante. DeForest respectfully requests consideration for appropriate coverage in Labour & Employment in Mexico.
editorial_development.b10:
DeForest’s Labour & Employment practice advises employers whose workforce stability is central to operational continuity. The team combines labour advisory, litigation, collective labour relations, social security, compliance and workforce governance for domestic and multinational businesses operating across Mexico.

The practice is particularly active in labour-intensive and regulated sectors, including automotive manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, logistics, technology, retail and financial services. Its work spans collective bargaining, union-representation disputes, workforce integration following acquisitions, employer substitutions, regulatory inspections, social-security matters, employment documentation, internal investigations and litigation portfolios involving large workforces and multiple jurisdictions.

The team’s recent matters include a post-acquisition labour integration across six Mexican states for more than 5,000 employees; collective labour strategies that prevented work stoppages; nationwide litigation portfolios comprising approximately 200 active proceedings; and labour and social-security governance for industrial operations employing approximately 17,000 people. The practice is led by Eduardo Garduño, with Javier Atzin Vallejo and Jaime Bustamante contributing experience in collective labour relations, litigation, compliance, social security and workforce governance.

matters.text:
Following Schaeffler’s global acquisition of Vitesco Technologies, DeForest was appointed to lead the post-acquisition labour integration in Mexico. The mandate involved harmonising employment structures while maintaining operational continuity across manufacturing facilities.

DeForest designed and implemented the labour integration strategy across Puebla, Estado de México, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Morelos and Chihuahua. The work standardised employment agreements, collective bargaining agreements, internal regulations, mixed commissions and labour-governance policies for a workforce exceeding 5,000 employees. The firm also manages 35 active labour proceedings involving suppliers and former employees, aligning litigation strategy with the unified post-acquisition governance model. Eduardo Garduño led the mandate.

DeForest represents Nueva Empresa, S.C. in two wrongful-termination proceedings involving a procedural dispute over recognition of the company’s attorney-in-fact. The labour court had refused to recognise the representation and issued an adverse ruling despite valid notarial documentation.

The firm brought constitutional amparo proceedings challenging the ruling. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney’s legal standing and restored the client’s right to present its defence. Javier Atzin Vallejo leads the ongoing matter, supported by Yrelia Barrón.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 1
matters.rawNotes:
Mextypsa, one of Mexico's leading engineering and infrastructure companies, relies on DeForest as its strategic labor counsel for projects where workforce governance is fundamental to successful execution. The firm's mandate extends beyond day-to-day employment advice, encompassing the design of labor structures capable of supporting large-scale infrastructure projects while preserving regulatory compliance and operational continuity throughout each project's lifecycle.

One of the most significant engagements involved the Guadalajara Metro Line 4 Project, a USD 552 million infrastructure development requiring a sophisticated labor framework to manage project-based recruitment, documentation, workforce administration and eventual demobilisation under intense public scrutiny. Simultaneously, DeForest represented the client in complex litigation arising from the Coahuila Wind Farm Project, where an adverse labor judgment threatened liabilities exceeding MXN 5.5 million.

Rather than treating these matters as isolated engagements, DeForest developed a comprehensive labor governance strategy combining preventive advisory with high-stakes dispute resolution. The team designed the contractual and compliance architecture supporting the Guadalajara Metro project, supervised workforce demobilisation to minimise post-project contingencies and successfully challenged the adverse labor judgment through constitutional proceedings, restoring the client's procedural rights and reopening the litigation.

Today, the firm manages more than twenty labor disputes for Mextypsa representing aggregate exposure of approximately MXN 21.5 million. Through early negotiation strategies and disciplined litigation management, DeForest has consistently reduced financial exposure while protecting operational continuity across the client's infrastructure portfolio.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 5
matters.rawNotes:
Nueva Empresa, S.C. engaged DeForest in two high-value wrongful termination proceedings that raised issues extending well beyond financial exposure. Following procedural objections concerning the legal standing of the company's attorney-in-fact, the labor court refused to recognise the company's representation, disregarded its defence and issued an adverse ruling despite the existence of valid notarial documentation confirming the attorney's legal identity.

The dispute presented a significant constitutional question concerning due process, legal certainty and the recognition of legally valid identity changes, creating an important opportunity to clarify procedural standards within Mexico's labor justice system.

DeForest challenged the ruling through constitutional amparo proceedings, arguing that the labor court's interpretation violated the client's due process rights and improperly disregarded legally recognised identity documentation. The Collegiate Court granted constitutional relief, ordered recognition of the attorney's legal standing and restored the client's right to present its defence.

Beyond the financial exposure of approximately MXN 3 million, the matter is significant for reinforcing constitutional protections governing procedural fairness and the legal recognition of identity, establishing an important precedent with broader implications for labor litigation in Mexico.

Against this exceptional backdrop, the employee retained DeForest to develop an alternative strategy capable of unlocking negotiations that had reached complete deadlock.

Rather than relying exclusively on litigation, DeForest designed a parallel mediation strategy running alongside the judicial proceedings. The strategy ultimately generated a series of favourable settlement agreements that preserved the employee's legitimate interests while significantly reducing systemic exposure for Enerflex and preventing PEMEX from facing joint liability arising from one of the largest labor awards ever issued in Mexico. The matter remains ongoing, with DeForest continuing to coordinate negotiations alongside PEMEX's in-house legal team.

This engagement reflects the firm's ability to resolve disputes where legal complexity, commercial interests and public-sector exposure intersect at the highest level.

matters.client: Volkswagen de México and VW Financial Services
matters.rawNotes:
Volkswagen de México, one of the country's largest industrial employers, together with Volkswagen Financial Services, continues to rely on DeForest to support the labor governance of its Mexican operations. The engagement spans complex employment matters affecting one of the most sophisticated manufacturing environments in the country, where regulatory certainty and workforce stability are fundamental to uninterrupted production.

DeForest manages active labor proceedings involving aggregate exposure approaching MXN 280 million while simultaneously advising on employment agreements, internal workplace regulations, disciplinary procedures, corporate powers of attorney and broader workforce governance initiatives across the client's operations in Puebla. Rather than treating litigation and advisory work separately, the firm provides an integrated governance model that combines dispute management with preventive labor strategy.

The long-standing relationship reflects the confidence placed in DeForest to support one of Mexico's most significant industrial employers through an increasingly complex labor and regulatory environment.
matters.teamMembers: José Alberto Díaz, Ana Ruiz, Erick Pérez and Ariam Barrientos.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 16
matters.rawNotes:
Robert Bosch de México operates one of the country's largest industrial workforces, employing approximately 17,000 people across multiple business divisions. Maintaining consistent labor governance within an organisation of this scale requires sophisticated employment structures capable of supporting operational efficiency while ensuring full regulatory compliance.

DeForest advises the client on the design and implementation of employment documentation, disciplinary procedures, labor governance policies and union-related matters, while also leading employer registration processes for Bosch Rexroth and coordinating social security structures across the organisation.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's ability to build and maintain labor governance platforms supporting complex industrial operations where workforce management directly influences operational continuity and long-term business performance.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 17
matters.rawNotes:
Coats de México engaged DeForest to support a significant workforce transformation affecting multiple manufacturing facilities across Puebla, Veracruz and Tlaxcala. The mandate required not only the redesign of the client's employment framework but also the careful management of sensitive collective labor issues capable of affecting manufacturing continuity.

The firm developed the client's labor architecture from the ground up, including employment agreements, labor policies, collective bargaining documentation and workforce governance protocols. Simultaneously, DeForest negotiated union-related matters involving exposure exceeding MXN 12.5 million while leading collective bargaining discussions that enabled the client to preserve operational stability throughout the restructuring process.

The engagement highlights the firm's ability to combine workforce transformation with sophisticated collective labor negotiations for major industrial employers.
matters.teamMembers: José Alberto Díaz and Maximiliano Hernández.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 19
matters.rawNotes:
Omron, a global leader in industrial automation and advanced manufacturing technologies, engaged DeForest to modernise its labor governance framework following the implementation of significant employment reforms in Mexico. The mandate focused on ensuring that the client's employment structures remained aligned with evolving regulatory obligations while supporting the operational flexibility required by a sophisticated manufacturing business.

The engagement required a comprehensive review of remote-work policies, employment documentation, labor compliance procedures and social security obligations within a rapidly changing regulatory environment.

DeForest redesigned the client's employment documentation, updated internal labor policies and implemented governance mechanisms supporting hybrid working arrangements, IMSS compliance and ongoing labor reform obligations. The firm also delivered practical guidance to management teams, enabling consistent implementation of the revised framework across the organisation.

Rather than responding to isolated compliance issues, DeForest developed a preventive governance model designed to minimise regulatory exposure while preserving the operational agility required by a global industrial business.
matters.teamMembers: José Alberto Díaz and Ana Ruíz.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 20
matters.rawNotes:
Benteler, one of the world's leading automotive suppliers, entrusted DeForest with one of the most sensitive labor challenges currently affecting industrial employers in Mexico: a union representativeness dispute capable of disrupting operations at one of its manufacturing facilities in Puebla. The matter arose within the broader transformation of Mexico's collective labor framework, where representation challenges increasingly influence business continuity across the automotive sector.

DeForest assumed responsibility for the client's strategic response, combining litigation, collective bargaining strategy and continuous negotiations with the competing unions. The firm's objective extended beyond resolving the legal dispute; it focused on preserving operational stability while ensuring full compliance with Mexico's labor legislation and respect for employees' collective rights.

Alongside the representation proceedings, DeForest continues strengthening the client's labor governance platform through the implementation of employment agreements, internal labor policies and collective bargaining documentation, reinforcing long-term organisational stability.
matters.teamMembers: José Alberto Díaz, Erick Pérez and Ariam Barrientos

matters.name: Confidential Matter 21
matters.rawNotes:
Grupo Radio Centro engaged DeForest to manage a highly sensitive internal employment investigation involving allegations against a senior executive. Beyond the immediate employment implications, the matter carried significant reputational risk for one of Mexico's best-known media organisations, requiring a careful balance between procedural integrity, confidentiality and organisational stability.

DeForest designed and supervised the internal investigation, coordinating evidence-gathering, legal analysis and strategic decision-making while ensuring compliance with applicable employment standards. Through an objective and carefully structured process, the firm prevented litigation valued at approximately MXN 750,000 while protecting the client's reputation during a particularly sensitive period.

The engagement illustrates the firm's ability to manage complex workplace investigations where legal, commercial and reputational considerations converge.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 23
matters.rawNotes:
Art Human, a financial services company active in real estate financing and executive search, relies on DeForest as external labor counsel for the management of its employment platform. Beyond active litigation, the client sought to strengthen internal governance while preparing the organisation for increasingly demanding labor and social security inspections.

DeForest manages the client's labor litigation portfolio while simultaneously conducting audits, strengthening internal controls, harmonising employment procedures and implementing preventive governance measures. The effectiveness of this approach was demonstrated when three separate inspections conducted by the Ministry of labor and IMSS concluded without the imposition of any fines, despite combined potential exposure approaching MXN 2 million.

The engagement demonstrates how preventive labor governance can substantially reduce regulatory exposure while supporting sustainable organisational growth.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 24
matters.rawNotes:
SKF Industrial, a global technology company specialising in bearings, seals and industrial engineering solutions, engaged DeForest to strengthen the legal framework supporting an operation of approximately 200 employees in Mexico. As a highly technical manufacturing business, the client required an employment structure capable of supporting operational discipline, regulatory compliance and consistent workforce governance across its industrial activities.

DeForest conducted a comprehensive review of the client's labor framework, redesigning internal workplace regulations, employment agreements, mixed commissions and labor policies to ensure full alignment with current Mexican labor legislation and the client's global governance standards.
Beyond updating documentation, the engagement established a preventive employment platform designed to reduce regulatory exposure, strengthen day-to-day workforce management and provide a legally robust framework capable of supporting the client's long-term industrial operations in Mexico.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 25
matters.rawNotes:
Corrugados y Empaques de Oriente, a Mexican manufacturer specialising in customised packaging solutions, retained DeForest to provide integrated labor and corporate legal support for its ongoing operations. Operating within a manufacturing environment where production continuity and workforce coordination are closely interconnected, the client required consistent legal support capable of aligning employment governance with broader corporate objectives.

DeForest acts as external strategic counsel across both labor and corporate matters, supporting workforce management, internal governance, contractual discipline and day-to-day operational decision-making. The integrated nature of the mandate allows the client to address employment and corporate matters under a unified legal strategy while strengthening the stability and scalability of its manufacturing platform.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's ability to provide multidisciplinary legal support for growing industrial businesses requiring coordinated labor and corporate advice.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 26
matters.rawNotes:
Shirushi, a regional restaurant group operating approximately twenty locations, engaged DeForest to support the labor governance of a business operating within one of the most labor-intensive sectors of the Mexican economy. High employee turnover, decentralised operations and the operational demands of the hospitality industry required a practical employment framework capable of supporting consistent workforce management across multiple sites.

DeForest advises the client across the full spectrum of labor matters, including employment documentation, workforce policies, disciplinary procedures and day-to-day employment advisory. The firm has implemented a preventive governance model designed to standardise employment practices across all restaurant locations while reducing litigation risk and strengthening regulatory compliance.

The engagement illustrates DeForest's ability to adapt sophisticated labor governance principles to operational environments characterised by high workforce mobility and continuous business activity.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 27
matters.rawNotes:
AUNDE, an international automotive supplier specialising in seating systems and technical textiles, retained DeForest to provide ongoing labor and social security advice supporting its manufacturing operations in Mexico. The mandate required coordinated legal assistance capable of addressing both workforce governance and regulatory compliance within a highly specialised industrial environment.

DeForest provides integrated advice across labor and social security matters, supporting employment structures, regulatory compliance and workforce administration while ensuring alignment with evolving labor legislation. By combining day-to-day advisory with preventive legal planning, the firm enables the client to maintain stable industrial operations while reducing long-term regulatory exposure.

The engagement reflects the firm's experience advising sophisticated automotive manufacturers operating under demanding labor and social security frameworks.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 28
matters.rawNotes:
Natividad Abogados, one of Mexico's leading specialist labor law firms, appointed DeForest as its regional correspondent counsel for labor litigation in central Mexico. The mandate reflects the confidence placed by a recognised market leader in DeForest's ability to represent clients in complex employment proceedings outside its principal jurisdiction.

DeForest manages approximately forty-five labor proceedings on behalf of Natividad Abogados, coordinating local litigation strategy, procedural management and court representation while ensuring consistency with the client's national legal approach.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's technical credibility within the legal market itself, acting as trusted regional counsel for one of Mexico's best-known labor law practices.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 29
matters.rawNotes:
Recicla Ambiente, a company operating approximately 700 employees across multiple Mexican states, engaged DeForest to support both its labor governance and collective labor strategy. The geographic dispersion of the workforce and the coexistence of multiple unions required coordinated legal management capable of maintaining consistent employment standards throughout the organisation.

DeForest advises the client across labor, collective bargaining and union negotiations in Puebla, Querétaro, Silao, Aguascalientes, Ramos Arizpe and Apodaca, coordinating employment strategy across multiple jurisdictions while supporting negotiations with different unions according to local operational requirements.

The engagement highlights the firm's ability to manage geographically dispersed workforces through integrated labor governance and sophisticated collective labor strategy.

matters.name: Confidential Matter 30
matters.rawNotes:
SEBNMX, an automotive manufacturer employing approximately 2,000 people in Tlaxcala, engaged DeForest to modernise the legal framework supporting one of its principal manufacturing operations. The mandate arose within the context of Mexico's labor reform, requiring the client to strengthen its employment governance while maintaining uninterrupted industrial operations.

DeForest conducted a comprehensive review of the client's labor governance platform, updating internal workplace regulations, employment agreements, labor policies and mixed commissions while supporting the implementation of the latest labor reform requirements. The engagement focused on ensuring that the client's employment framework remained operationally effective, legally compliant and capable of supporting a large industrial workforce.

By integrating legal compliance with practical workforce governance, the firm strengthened the client's long-term organisational resilience while reducing regulatory exposure.

matters.name: Matter 31
matters.rawNotes:
SCOTCH engaged DeForest to review and restructure its corporate and labor framework following the introduction of Mexico's specialised services regime (REPSE). The matter required a multidisciplinary approach combining labor, corporate and regulatory expertise to ensure that the client's business model remained fully aligned with the country's evolving outsourcing framework.

Working jointly across its corporate and labor practices, DeForest carried out a comprehensive review of the client's corporate structure, specialised services model, bylaws and REPSE registration while simultaneously conducting an audit of more than eighty suppliers to determine the appropriate regulatory treatment of specialised services agreements.

The engagement demonstrates the firm's ability to advise clients on complex regulatory transformations where employment, corporate governance and commercial operations converge.
